subject: PoC next steps — deployment mode & trial plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@acme-corp.com>; Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC next steps — deployment mode & trial plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for walking us through the integration points and the latency/throughput targets. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the proposed next steps so we can align on the right PoC approach and deployment mode: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput), or Private VPC/on-prem (data residency).

High-level proposed PoC (attached draft):
- Objective: Validate inference latency & cost at 100 RPS with 512-token context across a representative subset of prompts.
- Success criteria:
  - p95 token latency <= 250ms for standard generative calls
  - End-to-end inference cost target <$0.01 per 1k tokens (TBD based on batch config)
  - No PII leakage on test dataset; pass basic security checklist
- Timeline: 3-week trial (1 week setup, 1 week run, 1 week analysis/roundup)
- Stakeholders: Samantha (Platform), Tom (ML infra), Jordan (Redwood AE), Ben (SE), Marissa (Customer Success)
- Suggested deployment mode for the PoC: start on Hosted API to get fast results and collect metrics, then if you need consistent capacity or private networking we can transition to Dedicated or Private VPC for the validation run.

Action items for Acme:
1) Confirm the list of 20 sample prompts and a small test dataset (anonymized).
2) Confirm whether you require private networking for the PoC (VPC peering) or if Hosted API is acceptable to start.
3) Provide contact for procurement for any temporary reservation if you want Dedicated capacity during the PoC.

I attached a short PoC plan and a deployment-mode comparison sheet. Ben and Marissa are looped for technical and ops inputs.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]
[attachment: ACME_PoC_plan_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Samantha Liu <samantha@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC next steps — deployment mode & trial plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Thanks Jordan — really helpful summary. Quick answers:

1) We can provide the 20 sample prompts by EOD Friday (we'll anonymize first).
2) For risk/compliance we prefer to start with Hosted API for the initial functional validation, but if latency/cost looks promising we'll want to run the validation on Dedicated capacity (or Private VPC if security requires).
3) Procurement: I can connect you with our procurement lead, Priya Shah (procurement@acme-corp.com). We'll likely want a short-term reserved capacity for the full validation run if Dedicated is the path.

Couple of clarifying Qs:
- Does Redwood provide a short-term Dedicated reservation (1 month) for PoCs, or is that a longer-term commit?
- For Private VPC, what is the expected setup time? Any network/IP whitelisting needed in advance?

Samantha
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@acme-corp.com>; Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC next steps — deployment mode & trial plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Thanks Samantha — short answers to your questions:

- Short-term Dedicated: Yes — we can provision a 4-week Dedicated pool for POCs. It requires a short reservation (monthly billing) but we can do a trial-friendly arrangement; I'll coordinate the pricing/credit side with Marissa.
- Private VPC setup: Typical setup time is 2-3 weeks (network handshakes, routing, and KMS integration). We do need IP ranges for whitelisting and a contact for network engineering on your side.

Tech notes for your team to consider (for Hosted-first approach):
- For 100 RPS at 512 tokens, we recommend an initial batching config of 8-16 with prefix caching enabled; this usually hits latency targets while keeping cost down.
- If p95 latency under Hosted is > 300ms we suggest switching to a Dedicated pool with an optimized kernel profile.

I'll attach a short runbook snippet in the deployment XLS for the SE-run.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Tom

- We can provision a 4-week Dedicated trial reservation; Marissa will follow up with pricing/credit options and procurement steps.

Next immediate steps: 
1) Samantha to share sample prompts and anonymized dataset by EOD Friday.
2) Tom to send IP ranges / confirm whether Hosted is OK for initial run.
